changes: No substantive changes; notes expanded: era inferred as VS from bare 'saṃvata' plus the catalogue, and Pauṣa śukla 12 VS 1844 falls in Dec 1787/Jan 1788.

notes: The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Śaktihari', but the words after 'liṣitaṃ' ('śaktir hareḥ kuṃḍalinī prasiddhā svaciṃtyarupā graharāśidehā | tanvādibhāvān parikalpayaṃtī bhramaty ajasraṃ pravahānilena || 1 ||') are a complete Upajāti verse on Hari's power, made of the planets and signs and revolving on the pravaha wind. They are not a personal name, so no scribe or other person is named. The colophon has only 'saṃvata', with no era named. VS is assumed from the Devanagari script and the catalogue. Pauṣa śukla 12 of VS 1844 falls around late Dec 1787 or early Jan 1788.
